value: Effective January 1, 2027
detail: DHCS states that starting January 1, 2027, some adults (19-64 who get Medi-Cal through the ACA expansion) will need to work, volunteer, go to school, or be in training to keep Medi-Cal; Medi-Cal will send a letter if this applies.

value: MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1) plus applicable 1115 populations
detail: DHCS implementation materials define the subject population as the MAGI New Adult Group (ACA adult expansion), including adults covered under the state expansion for immigrants.

item: Ways to meet the rule (DHCS member materials)
value: Work and earn at least $580/month; seasonal work averaging $580/month over 6 months; job training 80 hours/month; volunteering or community service 80 hours/month; school at least half-time; or a mix totaling 80 hours or $580
detail: DHCS member-facing list of qualifying options; the DHCS outreach letter to members states income can be from any source.
notes: See flagged items: member page says work at a job and earn at least $580, while the MEDIL outreach letter says income from any source. The controlling measurement is MAGI-based monthly income under 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) and Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6) (see WR-05/FL-06).

value: Outreach letters mailed from late August 2026; member letter states the rules will not go into effect until March 2027
detail: The DHCS outreach letter tells current members the Work and Community Engagement Rule and 6-Month Renewal Rule will not go into effect until March 2027; counties must include the outreach letter with application materials from October 1 through December 31, 2026.
notes: New applicants are subject to the requirement from the January 1, 2027 implementation date; see flagged items for the date framing.

value: Starting March 1, 2027
detail: Some members (adults 19-64 in the ACA expansion group) will have eligibility checked twice a year instead of once; missing deadlines can cause loss of coverage.
notes: CMS issued guidance (SMD #26-001, March 2026) on six-month renewals.

value: Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026; signed by Governor Newsom September 14, 2026
detail: Amends Welfare and Institutions Code 14005.69. Requires systems/data-first verification (wage data, aid codes, claims/encounter data, CDSS data) with minimal information requests; county must ask the person to confirm information when reliable sources conflict before adverse action; coverage continues during the 30-day noncompliance period (at renewal, active eligibility at least through the end of that month); notice deemed received 5 days after its date and self-attested non-receipt is good cause; before denial/disenrollment the county must check every other basis of Medi-Cal or insurance-affordability eligibility and offer a fair hearing. Implementation conditions: the work-rule duty applies no sooner than Jan. 1, 2027 and after DHCS confirms systems are programmed; the section is implemented only after the director's written systems determination to Finance, only with needed federal approvals/FFP, and DHCS may defer a change that needs an unmade additional appropriation (subd. (q)-(r)); regulations due by July 1, 2029 (subd. (o)(2)).
notes: Signing recorded on the Governor's site (gov.ca.gov, September 14, 2026). Full chaptered text re-verified 2026-10-18.

value: From January 1, 2027
detail: Medi-Cal will pay fewer past medical bills: adults 19-64 without children get one month of retroactive coverage; everyone else gets two months.

value: From October 1, 2028
detail: Some adults 19-64 (not pregnant, not on Medicare, making more than $15,560 a year per the DHCS member page) may owe copayments for certain services, capped at 5 percent of household income per year; no copays for emergency care, checkups, pregnancy care, pediatric care, mental health and substance use treatment, or community clinic services.
notes: The $15,560 figure does not match 2025 ($15,650) or 2026 ($15,960) 100% FPL for one person - flagged for review.

value: Up to 233,000 members may lose coverage by June 2027; about 1 million by January 2028; about 1.4 million by June 2028
detail: DHCS stakeholder presentation estimates (February 2026); all numbers are estimates and subject to change.

item: No work requirement in effect today
value: Medi-Cal currently does not require beneficiaries to work to be eligible
detail: The LAO notes Medi-Cal has no work requirement today; DHCS member materials place the work rules under January 2027.
source_name: CA Senate Budget Committee LAO handout (Feb 11, 2026)

value: Two modalities required by H.R. 1
detail: States must send outreach through at least two modalities (mail or electronic notice plus at least one more method); DHCS began a staggered text campaign in February 2026 and mailing outreach notices in late August 2026.

value: CMS initial guidance December 2025; CMS interim final rule June 1, 2026 (effective July 31, 2026)
detail: DHCS tracks both the December 2025 CMS information bulletin and the June 2026 interim final rule (Federal Register June 3, 2026) on its federal impact page.
source_name: DHCS - Tracking Federal Impact: Medi-Cal Eligibility

value: Applicant: 1 month immediately before applying. Enrollee: any 1 month since last determination
detail: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d)(1)-(2) (AB 2161). ACWDL 25-30 renewal examples confirm one qualifying month in the look-back period is enough and qualifying months need not be consecutive; at application the county verifies the month immediately prior (look-back month). Counties do not reassess on a change-in-circumstance report alone.
source_name: California Legislative Information - AB 2161 (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d))
notes: Key planning fact for variable income: at renewal, a single month with MAGI-based income of at least $580 (or 80 qualifying hours, or half-time school) in the period satisfies the California test, per current law/preliminary guidance.

value: Existing members may return without a new application within 90 days once compliance is shown
detail: ACWDL 25-30 Step 4: existing Medi-Cal members discontinued for work-rule noncompliance may return to coverage without a new application during the 90-day cure period once they provide information demonstrating compliance; after 90 days they can re-apply at any time. Before any denial/discontinuance the county must first evaluate eligibility for all other Medi-Cal programs not subject to the requirement.
notes: Preliminary county guidance; confirm current county procedure on the notice of action.

item: Statutory income test for the work requirement
value: Total monthly income, using MAGI-based financial methods, for the individual's MAGI-based household budget, at or above the federal minimum wage (29 U.S.C. 206) x 80 hours
detail: WIC 14005.69(e)(6), as amended by AB 2161: the individual has 'a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods, as specified in Section 1396a(e)(14) of Title 42 of the United States Code, for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 of the United States Code, multiplied by 80 hours.'
notes: California statute frames the test on MAGI-based income; ACWDL 25-30 describes it as 'total gross income'. See flagged items FL-05, FL-06 and FL-16.

value: One month immediately preceding the month of application
detail: WIC 14005.69(d)(1): 'An applicable individual who applies for the Medi-Cal program shall demonstrate work or community engagement for one month immediately preceding the month during which the individual applies for the Medi-Cal program.'

value: Any one month between the most recent determination and the next regularly scheduled redetermination
detail: WIC 14005.69(d)(2): an enrolled individual 'shall demonstrate work or community engagement for any one month during the period between the individual's most recent determination or redetermination... and their next regularly scheduled redetermination of eligibility.'

value: 30 calendar days from receipt of the notice; Medi-Cal services continue for enrolled members; active eligibility maintained for renewing members until at least the last day of the month of the 30-day period
detail: WIC 14005.69(k)(1)(B) and (C): the county must provide 30 calendar days beginning when the notice of noncompliance is received, continue to provide Medi-Cal services during that period for enrolled individuals, and for an individual renewing during a six-month redetermination period 'maintain active eligibility pending verification... until at least the last day of the month of the 30-calendar-day period.'

item: Required checks before any denial or disenrollment
value: Determine every other basis for Medi-Cal eligibility or another insurance affordability program, and give written notice plus a fair-hearing opportunity
detail: WIC 14005.69(k)(1)(E), as amended by AB 2161: 'Before denying the applicable individual's application or disenrolling the individual, the county shall first do both of the following: (i) Determine whether there is any other basis for eligibility for the Medi-Cal program or for another insurance affordability program for the individual. (ii) Provide written notice and grant the individual an opportunity for a fair hearing.'
notes: Subdivision (n) separately requires the department to consider all other bases of eligibility under the Medi-Cal state plan before denying coverage.

value: Verify through wage data, Medi-Cal aid codes, claims and encounter data, Department of Social Services data, and consent-based verification platforms
detail: WIC 14005.69(c), as amended by AB 2161, requires DHCS to confirm systems are programmed to maintain coverage with minimal information requests by verifying compliance through interfaces with those data sources and by allowing individuals to add information through consent-based verification platforms.
notes: ACWDL 25-30 adds Equifax as an income-verification source and requires counties to accept electronically verified exemptions without further documentation.

item: Notice delivery formats required by state law
value: Regular mail or elected electronic format, plus one or more additional forms
detail: WIC 14005.69(l)(2), as amended by AB 2161: notice 'shall be delivered by regular mail or, if elected by the individual, in an electronic format, and shall be delivered in one or more additional forms, which may include telephone, text message, an internet website, other commonly available electronic means.'

value: Implement the federal requirement in the way that is least administratively burdensome to applicants and beneficiaries
detail: WIC 14005.69(a), as amended by AB 2161: 'It is the intent of the Legislature that the department implement work or community engagement requirements... to ensure that all eligible Medi-Cal applicants and beneficiaries obtain and maintain coverage in ways that are least administratively burdensome to applicants and beneficiaries.'

value: WIC 14005.69 remains operative only as long as 42 U.S.C. 1396a(xx) is operative
detail: WIC 14005.69(p), as amended by AB 2161: 'This section shall remain operative only as long as Section 1396a(xx) of Title 42 of the United States Code (Section 71119 of federal H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21)) is operative.'
notes: Subdivision letters follow the AB 2161 chaptered text. The consolidated code display at leginfo currently ends at subdivision (n), so this letter cannot be confirmed from the display; see flagged items FL-28 and FL-29. The quoted requirement is unchanged either way. Subdivision letters are from the AB 2161 chaptered text (the operative amending act). Leginfo's consolidated display still shows the earlier SB 164 wording and different letters; see FL-28.

value: $130,000 for one person through June 30, 2027; $21,000 for one person from July 1, 2027
detail: DHCS member page: through June 30, 2027 the asset limit is $130,000 for one person plus $65,000 for each additional person (up to 10); starting July 1, 2027 it is $21,000 for one person, $31,000 for two, plus $1,550 for each additional person. Assets that count include bank accounts, cash, and more than one house or vehicle; the home you live in, one vehicle, household items, and some savings such as retirement accounts do not count.
notes: Applies only to non-MAGI groups (65+, disability, nursing home, families over the MAGI income limits). MAGI adult expansion enrollment has no asset test - see MC-08.

value: Some members will pay a monthly premium to keep full-scope Medi-Cal; non-payment converts coverage to restricted scope
detail: DHCS member page: starting July 1, 2027, some members will need to pay a premium to keep full-scope Medi-Cal. If unpaid, coverage changes to restricted scope (emergency care, pregnancy-related care, nursing home care). Children 0-18, pregnant people (through pregnancy and one year after), and former foster youth under 26 will not have to pay.
notes: Tied to immigration-status groups; DHCS directs readers to its immigration-status chart. Not applicable to U.S. citizens, but published for completeness.

value: Section 71120 of P.L. 119-21 (new Social Security Act 1916(k)) requires states to impose cost sharing above $0 and not more than $35 per item or service starting October 1, 2028, with total family cost sharing capped at 5% of family income
detail: CMCS Informational Bulletin (November 18, 2025): “Under new section 1916(k) of the Act, states must impose such cost sharing beginning October 1, 2028. Cost sharing imposed under this section cannot exceed $35 for any care, item, or service… Aggregate out-of-pocket costs for all individuals in the family cannot exceed 5 percent of the income of the family.” DHCS's H.R.1 Implementation Plan lists the same October 1, 2028 effective date.
source_name: CMS CMCS Informational Bulletin: Summary of Working Families Tax Cut Legislation (Nov. 18, 2025)
notes: The DHCS member page states the 5% annual cap and an income threshold of $15,560 but does not state the $35 per-service maximum; see FL-07 for the threshold discrepancy (the figure matches no published federal poverty guideline). Replacement made in the 2026-10-18 pass because the previously cited DHCS document does not state the $35 maximum.

value: Medi-Cal eliminated member cost sharing on July 1, 2022; DHCS plans nominal copayment amounts and a no-denial-for-nonpayment rule
detail: DHCS H.R.1 Implementation Plan: 'Prior to July 1, 2022 when cost-sharing for members was eliminated, Medi-Cal imposed nominal copayments (generally $1)... To implement this provision, DHCS will similarly establish nominal copayment amounts... DHCS will clarify what services are subject to copayments, that services cannot be denied for lack of payment.'

item: Budget Act coverage-loss projection (update to CA-09)
value: 2026-27 Budget Act projects total H.R. 1 disenrollment of 44,000 in 2026-27 and 1.3 million by 2029-30
detail: DHCS 2026-27 Budget Act Highlights: 'The Budget projects total H.R. 1 disenrollment of 44,000 in 2026-27 and 1.3 million by 2029-30.' The same document reports the work and community engagement requirement reduces the budget by $357.6 million ($90.3 million General Fund) in 2026-27 and $9.6 billion ($2.4 billion General Fund) over the period.
notes: Projections differ from the February 2026 SAC estimates in CA-09 (233,000 by June 2027; 1 million by January 2028; 1.4 million by June 2028). Both are DHCS estimates from different dates; neither supersedes the other.

item: Six-month renewal mechanics for new applicants
value: Renewal set six months from the first month of eligibility; 30 days to return information, two reminder letters, and a 90-day cure period
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-31: individuals approved for the MAGI New Adult Group on or after January 1, 2027 have their renewal set six months from the first month of eligibility. The six-month process follows existing annual renewal procedures including automated and manual ex parte reviews, a prepopulated renewal form, a 30-day timeframe for enrollees to verify additional information, two reminder letters, timely notice, and a 90-day cure period.

value: Any coverage group other than the MAGI New Adult Group; American Indians and Alaska Natives; pregnant or 12-month postpartum individuals; children under 19
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-31 lists these populations as continuing on annual (12-month) renewal. Parent/caretaker relatives and Medi-Cal Inmate Eligibility Program members inside the MAGI New Adult Group are NOT exempt from six-month renewals unless they meet another exemption (for example pregnancy or tribal status).
notes: A parent/caretaker relative of a child 13 or younger is exempt from the work requirement but still renews every six months.

item: Statute that added Welfare and Institutions Code 14005.69
value: SB 164 (Chapter 27, Statutes of 2026, effective June 29, 2026); AB 2161 (Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026, effective September 14, 2026) amended it
detail: Leginfo's consolidated code display for WIC 14005.69 carries the history note: “Added by Stats. 2026, Ch. 27, Sec. 75. (SB 164) Effective June 29, 2026. Conditionally operative as prescribed by its own provisions.” AB 2161 is “An act to amend Section 14005.69 of the Welfare and Institutions Code,” so it amended rather than added the section.
notes: Resolves flagged item FL-26. The consolidated code display currently shows the SB 164 text; use the chaptered AB 2161 text for the September 14, 2026 amendments.
